meta_thesis: This is a tempo meta patch: Valve gutted comeback souls and the Unstable Rift's early-game generosity, so winning lane and snowballing now actually converts into winning the game. Scaling carries (Wraith, Celeste, gun Haze builds, Warden builds) lose their safety net, while early-game tempo/snowball heroes (Paige, Apollo, Vindicta, Yamato, Silver, Holiday) rise. The biggest movers are system changes — economy, rift, parry, reload, slows, melee cycle time — not the hero number tweaks.

hero_claims.why: No direct changes, but he is one of the best early-game snowballers (ganks, wins lane, kills jungle instantly, escapes death, high flat damage/healing) and tempo now matters. The creator calls him 'super buffed this patch' despite being absent from the notes.
Only tweaked, same character, but the dash/light-melee no longer interrupting gun cycle time lets him weave dashes and punches between shots for a more fluid lane.
Nerfed seven different ways with no buffs, but the bigger hits are indirect: egg nerf, her item nerfs, scaling nerfs punishing early-game losers, and slows now affecting air drag hurting her flying.
Described as the same character; no meaningful opinion beyond that.
Gun Haze is better now with an appreciable damage increase since her damage comes from Fixation stacks, so headshots matter more; viability unclear but promising.
Being made more of a gun hybrid and lasso buffed; with tempo up and post-20-minute picks more valuable (respawn timer change), she should re-emerge with hybrid gun-spirit builds.
Slight nerfs, which the creator approves of because the character is overpowered.
Frozen Shelter now has innate spirit power, so it may be usable late game without maxing it; creator wants to test builds that don't max the ability.
Slight direct buffs, but mostly rises because the characters she competes with were nerfed.
Gun Lash killed in favor of stomp Lash, which the creator calls great and healthy — ground-strike Lash is back.

Triple-dip buffed: direct buffs, tempo being more important (she is a strong tempo character), and flying/flyers being nerfed so fewer Celeste/Vindicta-style threats. Creator calls her one of the biggest winners and a monster.

Knives no longer ricochet but do more current-HP damage, giving him more anti-tank killing ability — a healthy change; alt-fire now actually damages people again after past over-nerf.

Weighted Bola acting as Phantom Strike is massive; cycle-time change improves lane and mid-game fights, plus better scaling and sprint speed. Creator expects her to merge into the meta alongside Yamato.
Ultimate now works with ricochet and split shot simultaneously — a buff — but the main buff is tempo mattering and super-scaling being nerfed, since she is a high-tempo early gun carry.
Nerfed across the board; every ability did too much damage. Still picked for the same identity reasons but no longer randomly tops damage while building half support items.
Slight nerf, same character.

Nerfed across the board (bullet damage per boon, flask range/speed, Willpower debuff resistance), amplified by item nerfs and carry/scaling nerfs. Not gutted — silence cage keeps him viable — but should settle to a balanced win rate rather than 55%.
Nerfed as a scaler (healing, armor shred, slow) and her items dipped, plus Plated Armor becoming a great anti-Wraith item; less oppressive mainly from tempo buffs and scaling nerfs, not a gutting.
Buffed again and benefits from the tempo change; creator expects a huge uptick in play as players start practicing her again.

reasoning_patterns: Reads a system change's effect through win-conversion: the early Unstable Rift comeback nerf means a lane-winning team can now contest the rift, which both denies comeback souls and turns early leads into wins — so 'tempo' is buffed indirectly.

Frames an economy redistribution as a player-behavior fix: routing excess comeback souls to the two lowest-econ players is read as killing the AFK-farming carry who out-farmed the winning team, an explicitly high-ELO problem.
Argues a hero absent from the notes is the biggest winner: Apollo has no patch lines, but tempo mattering makes his early-game kit 'super buffed' — absence from notes is not absence of change.
Separates direct vs indirect nerfs: Celeste and Wraith are 'less nerfed by their own lines than by' scaling nerfs, item nerfs, and slows now affecting air drag.
Reads an item's hidden synergy: the air-drag slow change turns Life Strike's big slow into real CC, and Plated Armor's bug fix turns it into an anti-mixed-damage counter item.
Labels a double-dip nerf: Golden Goose Egg is hit by the tempo shift and by direct nerfs, and counting stored souls toward net worth makes it unbuyable.

patch_calls.headline: Comeback souls and the Unstable Rift gutted to restore tempo — the most significant balance patch in a year, bigger than the AP reworks.
non_obvious_calls: Apollo is not in the notes but is one of the best characters now because he is a top snowballer; notes absence hides his buff.
Comeback souls above enemy team average net worth are redistributed to the two lowest-econ players via tick gold, directly nerfing the farming carry in high ELO.
Respawn timers increased only after 20 minutes, raising the value of picks and making Mid Boss easier to take between 20-30 minutes.
Stuns now pause reload instead of cancelling it (Seven's static charge no longer resets your reload), and parry now pauses reload and cancels dash momentum.
Slows now affect air drag, making movement-speed-slow a genuinely important stat and hurting flyers like Celeste and Vindicta.
Dashes and light melees no longer interrupt gun cycle time, giving Abrams and Silver smoother lane weaving.
Breakables spawning later is a bigger nerf to Calico than to Rem, contrary to the common read.
Permanent objectives' bounty increased, making them better relative to Rift and urn.
Rem's breakable timing and bug fixes are not the huge Rem nerf people assume.
